G ospe l singer Moses Bliss has shared a video featuring his wife, Marie Bliss, amid rumours of a marital crisis involving the couple. The speculation began after blogs reported that the couple, who married in March 2024 and have a son, were considering divorce over undisclosed marital issues. In what appeared to be a response to the rumours, Moses Bliss took to his Instagram page on November 17, 2026, to share a video featuring himself and his wife. In the clip, the couple were seen walking closely together and enjoying a night out at an upscale venue before the singer gently helped Marie into a waiting black SUV. He accompanied the video with a brief caption: “Serenity.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. The post attracted significant attention after entertainment accounts interpreted it as a subtle response to the speculation about the couple’s marriage. This is not the first time such rumours have surfaced. Similar speculation emerged in August 2026, and the couple’s previous response also involved sharing joint content rather than issuing direct public statements. However, some celebrities criticised the singer’s approach to addressing the rumours. I could have had three private jets if I yielded to temptation – Frank Edwards Davido’s wedding shot me into limelight — Cinematographer, Durode Akintante ‘I find this disrespectful,’ Sola Allyson rebukes fan over comment Reacting to Moses Bliss’s Instagram video in a post on X on November 18, 2026, media personality and hype man Oladotun Kayode, popularly known as Do2dtun, criticised the singer for sharing a romantic video amid the breakup rumours. He warned that trying to appease social media users could validate the speculation and make the singer appear guilty. Do2dtun argued that rushing online to prove that a marriage was intact could achieve the opposite effect, cautioning that attempts to appease social media critics could create a slippery slope. He wrote, “If he isn’t careful, he will slide into that net gradually. Whoever advised him to do this didn’t tell him; this makes him look more guilty to be honest. “Nigerian entertainers need a good P.R, or social media manager. They don’t know how to kill a narrative or news. This move validates the rumour.” Do2dtun’s argument was that the timing of the post worked against Bliss rather than in his favour, suggesting that engaging with unverified speculation, even indirectly, could inadvertently lend it credibility. Some fans, however, supported the singer’s public display of affection and prayed for the couple’s marriage to remain intact. One Instagram user, iam_jayni\_, wrote, “Best response ever. God won’t let their wish come to pass.” Others echoed the prayer, while heron9010 added, “Father, we soak and cover this marriage with your precious blood.” Naomi Chima Naomi Chima is an entertainment and lifestyle correspondent at Punch Newspapers with over three years of experience.
